aphid.name: Aphids
aphid.cause: Small sap-sucking insects that cluster on new growth and undersides of leaves; thrive in warm, dry weather
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen which encourages soft new growth
Use yellow sticky traps to monitor early
organic: Spray neem oil solution every 7 days
Strong water spray to dislodge colonies
mechanical: Remove and destroy heavily infested shoots

chemical.warning: Only use if organic controls fail and infestation is severe
chemical.phi: Follow label pre-harvest interval, typically 7–14 days

earlyblight.name: Early Blight
earlyblight.cause: Fungal disease (Alternaria) favoured by warm, humid conditions and leaf wetness
prevention: Rotate crops, avoid planting tomato/potato repeatedly in same field
organic: Neem oil as a preventive spray
mechanical: Prune lower infected leaves and destroy them

chemical.warning: Apply preventively, not after heavy infection

fruitborer.name: Fruit Borer
fruitborer.cause: Moth larvae that bore into fruit and shoots
prevention: Use pheromone traps to monitor and trap adult moths
Remove and destroy damaged fruit promptly
Intercrop with marigold as a trap crop
mechanical: Hand-pick and destroy infested fruit/shoots

chemical.warning: Rotate chemical classes to avoid resistance

wilt.name: Bacterial/Fusarium Wilt
wilt.cause: Soil-borne bacteria or fungus blocking water transport in the plant
prevention: Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
mechanical: Remove and destroy wilted plants immediately, do not compost

chemical.warning: Focus on prevention and resistant varieties

lateblight.name: Late Blight
lateblight.cause: Fungus-like pathogen (Phytophthora) spreading fast in cool, wet, humid weather
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation in cool weather
mechanical: Destroy infected foliage immediately

chemical.warning: Apply before rain in high-risk weather, resistance can develop

cutworm.name: Cutworm
cutworm.cause: Caterpillars that cut young stems at soil level, active at night
prevention: Deep ploughing before planting exposes larvae to predators/sun
mechanical: Place collars around stems of young transplants

chemical.warning: Use only as last resort, harmful to soil organisms

thrips.name: Thrips
thrips.cause: Tiny slender insects that scrape and suck plant tissue, thrive in hot dry weather
prevention: Avoid water stress which increases susceptibility
mechanical: Remove weeds around field that host thrips

chemical.warning: Rotate with different chemical classes

purpleblotch.name: Purple Blotch
purpleblotch.cause: Fungal disease favoured by humid weather and dense planting
mechanical: Remove and destroy infected leaves

chemical.warning: Apply preventively in humid seasons

leafminer.name: Leaf Miner
leafminer.cause: Larvae that tunnel between leaf layers leaving pale winding trails
prevention: Remove and destroy affected leaves early
mechanical: Hand-pick and destroy mined leaves

chemical.warning: Only if infestation is severe

rootrot.name: Root Rot
rootrot.cause: Fungal disease in poorly drained, waterlogged soil
prevention: Improve drainage, raised beds in heavy soil
mechanical: Remove and destroy affected plants

chemical.warning: Prevention is more effective than cure

shootborer.name: Shoot & Fruit Borer
shootborer.cause: Moth larvae boring into shoots and fruit
prevention: Remove and destroy wilted shoot tips
mechanical: Prune and destroy infested shoots weekly

chemical.warning: Rotate chemical classes to manage resistance

anthracnose.name: Anthracnose (Fruit Rot)
anthracnose.cause: Fungal disease favoured by warm, humid, wet conditions
mechanical: Remove and destroy infected fruit

chemical.warning: Apply before heavy rain periods

whitefly.name: Whitefly
whitefly.cause: Tiny white flying insects that suck sap and spread viruses; secrete honeydew leading to sooty mould
mechanical: Vacuum or hose off light infestations

chemical.warning: Whitefly develops resistance quickly — rotate products

powderymildew.name: Powdery Mildew
powderymildew.cause: Fungal disease favoured by humid days and dry nights, poor air circulation
organic: Spray diluted milk or sulfur-based fungicide
mechanical: Remove and destroy heavily infected leaves

chemical.warning: Do not apply sulfur in very hot weather — can scorch leaves

jassid.name: Jassids (Leafhoppers)
jassid.cause: Small hopping insects that suck sap, causing leaf curling and yellowing

chemical.warning: Rotate chemical classes

yellowmosaic.name: Yellow Mosaic Virus
yellowmosaic.cause: Virus spread by whitefly, causing yellow mosaic patterning on leaves
organic: Neem oil to reduce whitefly vector
mechanical: Rogue out infected plants early in the season

chemical.active: No direct cure — manage the whitefly vector
chemical.warning: Focus on prevention and vector control

stemborer.name: Stem Borer
stemborer.cause: Moth larvae boring into stems causing "dead heart" in young plants
prevention: Avoid staggered planting near infested fields
organic: Bt spray at early larval stage
mechanical: Remove and destroy dead-heart tillers

chemical.warning: Apply at early larval stage for best effect

blast.name: Rice Blast
blast.cause: Fungal disease favoured by high humidity and excess nitrogen
mechanical: Remove infected plant debris after harvest

chemical.warning: Apply preventively at first sign of lesions

bph.name: Brown Plant Hopper
bph.cause: Sap-sucking insect causing "hopper burn" (patches of drying, brown plants)
prevention: Maintain alternate wetting-drying rather than constant flooding where feasible
organic: Encourage spiders and natural predators, minimize broad-spectrum sprays
mechanical: Drain field briefly to disrupt hopper breeding

chemical.warning: Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural predators

fallarmyworm.name: Fall Armyworm
fallarmyworm.cause: Caterpillar feeding inside the whorl of young maize plants
prevention: Monitor whorls regularly from early growth stage
organic: Apply Bt-based spray into the whorl
mechanical: Hand-pick larvae from whorls in small plots

chemical.warning: Apply directly into the whorl for best effect

rust.name: Wheat Rust
rust.cause: Fungal disease spreading via wind-blown spores in humid, mild weather
prevention: Timely sowing to avoid peak spore periods
organic: Limited organic options — prevention is key
mechanical: Remove volunteer wheat plants that harbor spores

chemical.warning: Apply at first sign for best control

shootfly.name: Shoot Fly
shootfly.cause: Fly larvae boring into young seedling stems causing "dead heart"
prevention: Timely sowing at start of season reduces risk
Higher seed rate to compensate for losses
organic: Neem seed kernel extract spray at seedling stage
mechanical: Remove and destroy dead-heart plants

chemical.active: Seed treatment with Thiamethoxam (as locally approved)
chemical.warning: Apply as seed treatment before sowing

downymildew.name: Downy Mildew
downymildew.cause: Fungus-like pathogen favoured by high humidity and leaf wetness
mechanical: Remove and destroy infected plants early

chemical.warning: Apply preventively before humid spells

podborer.name: Pod Borer
podborer.cause: Moth larvae feeding on flowers and boring into developing pods
prevention: Intercrop with sorghum as a trap border
mechanical: Hand-pick larvae in small plots

chemical.warning: Apply at early flowering for best effect

leafspot.name: Leaf Spot
leafspot.cause: Fungal disease favoured by humid weather and leaf wetness
mechanical: Remove severely affected leaves

chemical.warning: Apply preventively

sigatoka.name: Sigatoka Leaf Spot
sigatoka.cause: Fungal disease of banana leaves, worse in humid, high-rainfall conditions
prevention: Remove and destroy infected leaves regularly
mechanical: Deleaf infected leaves regularly

chemical.warning: Rotate fungicide classes to avoid resistance

nematode.name: Root-knot Nematode
nematode.cause: Microscopic soil worms causing root galls and reduced nutrient uptake
mechanical: Soil solarization before planting

chemical.warning: Restricted in many regions — check local regulations

fruitfly.name: Fruit Fly
fruitfly.cause: Flies lay eggs in ripening fruit; maggots develop inside causing rot
prevention: Use fruit fly traps with methyl eugenol lure
Collect and destroy fallen fruit promptly
organic: Bait traps with jaggery + insecticide in a container (not sprayed on fruit)
mechanical: Bag individual fruit with paper/net bags

chemical.warning: Use bait stations rather than blanket spraying

hopper.name: Mango Hopper
hopper.cause: Sap-sucking insect active during flowering, causing flower and fruit drop
prevention: Avoid dense canopy — prune for airflow

chemical.warning: Avoid spraying during open flowering to protect pollinators

ringspot.name: Papaya Ringspot Virus
ringspot.cause: Virus spread by aphids, causing ring-shaped spots on fruit and leaf distortion
organic: Neem oil to reduce aphid vector
mechanical: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately

chemical.active: No direct cure — manage the aphid vector
chemical.warning: Focus on prevention and vector control

mite.name: Spider Mite
mite.cause: Tiny mites that feed on leaf undersides, thriving in hot, dry conditions
prevention: Maintain adequate irrigation to reduce plant stress
organic: Spray undersides of leaves with water to disrupt mites
mechanical: Remove heavily infested leaves

chemical.warning: Rotate miticide classes to avoid resistance
